In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cumulative effects of road building, logging and hunting on the bird community of a tropical forest can be minimized by careful management of the logging and the road building, by restricting the width of the deforested roads and by limiting the hunting of the large vertebrates in the newly opened forest.

the impact of human activities on tropical rain forest avifauna can be minimized if the disturbance is limited to a few species of trees per hectare, the forest structure is not significantly altered and hunting is restricted to the most common species.
the impact of road building and logging on bird communities is highly dependent on the intensity and type of disturbance.

the most important factor in the long-term conservation of rain forest birds is the protection of large tracts of primary forest.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of logging and road opening in the rain forests of French Guiana are not as severe as those observed in the Amazon and other parts of the world, and that the bird community is able to recover in 15 years.
a large proportion of the bird community of the tropical rain forest can be preserved if the human disturbance is limited to a narrow band of forest around the roads.

, although the effects of logging and road construction on tropical rain forests and their avifauna can be severe, they are not necessarily irreversible and that a large number of bird species are still able to survive and even thrive in degraded rain forests.
